turns.assessment: The simultaneous ~66 ps DGD increase and pre-FEC BER rise across multiple independent channels, with no corresponding receive-power, OSNR, amplifier-power, or pump-current change, is the signature of a common fibre PMD/DGD impairment rather than loss, amplification, or client equipment failure. The shared aerial span in the S22-to-S16 direction (E23) best matches the affected receivers and persistent LOF/SD condition; the reverse-direction fibre is a much weaker directional alternative.

proposals.rationale: E23 is the aerial shared fibre span oms.S22-S16.span1. A persistent DGD rise directly explains the nearly identical +66 ps DGD excursions, increased pre-FEC BER, and resulting OTU LOF/SD across channels while optical power and OSNR remain unchanged.
E7 is the reverse-direction fibre in the same aerial section and could experience similar environmental stress, but its direction is less consistent with the distribution of affected receivers.
A filter penalty can degrade BER without changing power, but the documented mode affects one channel and does not naturally explain the common DGD increase across many channels.
